scheme_name: Pension for Agitators Who were Jailed for 7 Days or Injured During the Uttarakhand State Movement
description:
The Pension for Agitators Who were Jailed for 7 Days or Injured During the Uttarakhand State Movement is a welfare scheme initiated by the Government of Uttarakhand.

This scheme was launched on 1st November 2000.

The background of this scheme is rooted in the demand for the creation of a separate state of Uttarakhand from the larger state of Uttar Pradesh.

The movement for a separate state began in the late 1990s and gained significant momentum leading to the formation of Uttarakhand as the 27th state of India.

The state movement involved numerous protests and demonstrations where many individuals faced imprisonment or injuries.

The objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance to those individuals who participated in the movement and suffered as a result.

The scheme aims to recognize the sacrifices made by the agitators and provide them with a monthly pension as a form of support.

The specific target is to provide a pension to individuals who were jailed for at least seven days or were injured during the agitation.

Eligible beneficiaries can receive a monthly pension of ₹5,000.

The pension is intended to support the livelihood of those who contributed to the statehood movement.

Eligibility criteria for this scheme include individuals who were actively involved in the Uttarakhand state movement.

Applicants must have been jailed for a minimum of seven days during the agitation period.

Alternatively, individuals who sustained injuries during the protests are also eligible for the pension.

There is no specific age limit mentioned in the eligibility criteria.

However, applicants must provide proof of their involvement in the movement.

This proof can include documents such as arrest records or medical certificates indicating injuries sustained.

The application process involves several steps.

First, eligible individuals must obtain the application form from the official website of the Uttarakhand government or designated offices.

The form requires personal details such as name, address, and contact information.

Applicants must also provide details regarding their involvement in the movement.

This includes dates of imprisonment or medical records of injuries.

Once the form is completed, it must be submitted to the District Magistrate's office.

Supporting documents must be attached to the application.

These documents include identity proof and any relevant certificates.

After submission, the application will be reviewed by the authorities.

The review process may take several weeks.

Once approved, beneficiaries will receive their pension on a monthly basis.

The pension is disbursed directly into the bank accounts of the beneficiaries.

The disbursement typically occurs on the first week of every month.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Uttarakhand Department of Social Welfare.

The department is responsible for the overall administration and monitoring of the scheme.

Contact details for the department can be found on the official Uttarakhand government website.

The scheme has been beneficial for many individuals who played a crucial role in the statehood movement.

As of the latest reports, over 1,000 beneficiaries are receiving the pension.

The total financial outlay for this scheme is approximately ₹60 lakh annually.

This amount is allocated from the state budget specifically for the welfare of the agitators.

The scheme has been praised for recognizing the sacrifices made by individuals during the movement.

It serves as a reminder of the importance of social justice and support for those who fought for their rights.

The government has also organized awareness programs to inform potential beneficiaries about the scheme.

These programs aim to ensure that eligible individuals are aware of their rights and the benefits available to them.

The pension scheme reflects the commitment of the Uttarakhand government to honor the legacy of the statehood movement.

In addition to the pension, the government has also provided other forms of support to the families of agitators who lost their lives during the movement.

This includes financial assistance for education and healthcare.

The government continues to evaluate the scheme to ensure that it meets the needs of the beneficiaries effectively.

Feedback from beneficiaries is taken into account for any necessary improvements.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative by the government to support marginalized communities and individuals who have faced hardships.

Overall, the Pension for Agitators Who were Jailed for 7 Days or Injured During the Uttarakhand State Movement is a significant welfare initiative.

It not only provides financial support but also acknowledges the contributions of individuals to the formation of Uttarakhand.

The scheme is a vital step towards ensuring that the sacrifices made during the movement are not forgotten.

It highlights the importance of government support in recognizing and addressing historical injustices.

The scheme is expected to continue evolving to better serve the needs of its beneficiaries.

The government remains committed to ensuring that all eligible individuals receive the assistance they deserve.

This initiative is a testament to the ongoing efforts to promote social welfare and justice in the state of Uttarakhand.
